body:
Minutes:

- Issue 186: Method to Rename Entry: Kagami Rosylight raised a web compatibility issue regarding the `move` method on file system handles, noting that the method accepted both string and object types, which caused issues when objects were implicitly coerced into strings. Participants discussed using Web IDL to annotate interfaces to prevent this type of implicit conversion. Kagami Rosylight also noted that WebKit and Chrome currently have differing implementations for the `move` signature, and the group agreed that converging these implementations is desirable.
- Issue 11729: Menu Elements: The group discussed the proposal to advance "menu elements" to stage two. David Baron noted that previous feedback regarding the DOM structure had been addressed by switching to nesting rather than ID refs and commands. While some participants previously raised concerns regarding the "checkable" attribute API shape, there was consensus to advance the proposal to stage two, with the understanding that the API design remains open for continued discussion and is not considered finalized.
- Issue 10573: Declarative Shadow DOM Adopted Stylesheets Attribute: Kurt Catti-Schmidt requested stage three for the shadow adopted stylesheets attribute on template elements. The proposal sparked a debate regarding the necessity of the feature, with some participants arguing that existing mechanisms like `link` and `style` or future module-based loading should address these needs, and that the current proposal felt like it was "relitigating" the design of adopted stylesheets. Proponents argued that adopted stylesheets are an existing, interoperable standard and that providing a declarative way to use them is necessary to prevent "JavaScript-only" limitations. No formal consensus was reached, and the group agreed to continue the conversation asynchronously.
- HTML Streaming PR 12645 and PR 12583: Noam Rosenthal introduced two pull requests intended to support HTML streaming: PR 12645 for standardized file parsing and PR 12583 for integrating fragment parser options with trusted types. Noam Rosenthal requested that participants review these items while maintainers are on leave. Luke W volunteered to review the HTML streaming PR in the following week.
- Issue 10677: Canvas Extended Text Metrics: Stephen Chenney presented an updated proposal for canvas extended text metrics, focusing on the ability to split strings into component glyphs to support text animations and layout around shapes. The updated proposal suggests separating text clustering into a distinct API object to avoid embedding it within the existing text metrics infrastructure. Stephen Chenney noted that while the TAG previously objected based on accessibility concerns, this updated proposal removes features covered by HTML and canvas. Participants suggested seeking feedback from CSS experts regarding text formatting.
- Pull Request 11765: Navigation API Optimization: Noam Rosenthal presented a pull request to optimize the navigation API by ignoring duplicate navigations, a change requested by the loading team. The group is seeking second implementers, and Noam Rosenthal requested that Mozilla participants and Apple representatives review the pull request.
- Closing and Feedback Requests: Stephen Chenney requested that participants review the issues raised against the HTML and canvas proposal to provide additional feedback before the next meeting.
